   Vernon Housing Commission Agenda Report

Meeting Date:  June 11, 2025
From:  Daniel S. Wall, P.E., Director of Public Works
Department:  Public Works
Submitted by:  Rosemary Lozada, Management Analyst

Subject
Quarterly City Housing Report

Recommendation
Receive and file the 2025 Second Quarter City Housing Report.

Background
Staff will present the Quarterly City Housing report for the period September 2024 to May 2025.
The report will include information regarding rent, occupancy, and annual inspections of City-
owned housing.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

None.

1.  Selection of Chair and Vice Chair

  Interim City Clerk Harrington presented the staff report.

MOTION
  Commissioner Ybarra moved and Chair Goff seconded a motion to select

ORAL REPORTS

4.  Brief Reports, Announcements, or Directives to Staff

  Interim City Administrator Calleros announced the City Newsletter has been
  delivered to all households in the City and posted online for reference. Topics
  included New Vernon Developments, Vernon Rebranding, Earthquake
  Preparedness, an Exide Update, photo collection of recent community events and
  announcements about upcoming City outreach.

  Upcoming events included Career Day, Halloween Spooktacular, and Fall Harvest.

  Vice Chair Goff expressed appreciation to staff.

  Chair Nevarez thanked Vice Chair Goff for her service as Chair over the last two
  years.

ADJOURNMENT

  With no further business, Chair Nevarez adjourned the meeting at 6:13 p.m.

  PRESENTATIONS

  1.  Quarterly City Housing Report
  Recommendation:
  Receive and file the 2025 Second Quarter City Housing Report.

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report and accompanying
  PowerPoint.

  Commissioner Ybarra inquired about significant findings from the inspections, and
  Public Works Director Wall reported that the housing inspections revealed normal
  wear and tear, such as minor water leaks and caulking.

  MOTION
  Commissioner Lopez moved and Commissioner Edry seconded a motion to
  receive and file the 2025 Second Quarter City Housing Report. The question was
  called and the motion carried 6-0, Vice Chair Goff absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following item:

  2.  Meeting Minutes
  Recommendation: Approve the September 11, 2024, Regular Vernon Housing
  Commission Meeting Minutes.

  ORAL REPORTS

  3.  Brief Reports, Announcements, or Directives to Staff

  City Administrator Saeki addressed immigration concerns in light of the recent
  immigration enforcement activity, and he affirmed the City’s commitment to the principles
  of the California Values Act, reassuring the Commission and residents that the City and
  the Vernon Police Department do not inquire about immigration status or participate in
  federal immigration law enforcement actions. He shared that City staff, Mayor Merlo,
  Council Members Lopez and Larios participated in a press conference with City of Los
  Angeles Mayor Bass and thirty-three other communities to stand in solidarity with one
  another.
 Docusign Envelope ID: 8DC38CB3-69D6-4035-A73A-94AE6F659719

  Regular Vernon Housing Commission Meeting Minutes  Page 3 of 3
  June 11, 2025

  City Administrator Saeki announced several upcoming events, including the Vernon
  Reads! Giveaway event, an upcoming Blood Drive, and the National Night Out event. He
  encouraged Commissioners to spread the word that the City Clerk’s Department would
  continue to recruit to fill upcoming vacancies on the Green Vernon Commission, the
  Vernon CommUNITY Fund Grant Committee, and the Vernon Housing Commission.

  Lastly, he shared that the May Edition of the Resident Newsletter was delivered to all
  Vernon households, which included news on the redevelopment of the former Farmer
  John site. He reiterated Mayor Pro Tem Ybarra’s invitation and welcomed Commissioners
  to attend the June 17, 2025, City Council meeting to receive LA Metro’s detailed
  presentation on Metro Link Union Station Project Update.

  RECESS
  At 6:11 p.m., Chair Nevarez recessed the meeting to Closed Session.

  CLOSED SESSION

  4.  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation (1 potential matter)

  RECONVENE

  At 7 p.m., Chair Nevarez adjourned the Closed Session and reconvened the regular
  meeting.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  City Attorney Moussa reported that the Commission met in Closed Session,
  discussed the item on the agenda, provided direction to staff and took no
  reportable action.

  ADJOURNMENT

  With no further business, Chair Nevarez adjourned the meeting at 7 p.m.

  _____________________________
  JORGE NEVAREZ, JR., Chairperson
